plain_english: Jonet Meik is described as the wife of a Glasgow burgess whose forename is tentatively read Niniane. The opening says that the testament was given by her own mouth on [15?] February 1606 and that she died a number of days afterwards. The exact interval is not safely deciphered: the testament date should not be published as her death date.

The opening names the husband and Robert Glasgow as executors or intromitters. Robert is expressly called her son again in the disposition of the remaining goods and debts. This is direct mother–son wording, unlike the appearances of Glasgow-named debtors or other legatees.

The inventory and accounts contain trading or household goods, debts due to the household, liabilities and legacies. The exact commodities, sums and many personal names remain difficult. Marioun Glasgow appears in a legacy clause, but the following relationship word is not securely resolved.
The testament continues onto image 83 through its attestation and confirmation. The following Robesoun testament is a different estate.
findings: Image 82 opening, lines 4–8: [15?] February 1606 is attached to the oral testament; death is described as days afterwards. A precise death date remains unresolved.

Image 82 opening line 6 and image 83 residue clause: Robert Glasgow is explicitly “hir sone”. This supports the mother–son relationship, without proving every other Glasgow named in the account related.
Image 83 first line: Marioun Glasgow’s relationship word remains nycht[?]; do not silently expand it to niece or assign a kinship link.
Image 82 account sections distinguish debtors, creditors and legatees. A repeated surname is not sufficient to identify an existing profile.
Image 83 confirmation: August 1607 is readable; the proposed xxvij/27 remains qualified in this review.
changes_from_previous: Expanded the earlier six-line selection to working readings across the opening, inventory, debts, legacies, attestation and confirmation.
Clarified that February 1606 wording dates the making of the testament, with death subsequent; it does not securely supply an exact death date.
Confirmed repeated explicit son wording for Robert; retained doubts about the husband’s forename, Marioun’s relationship and confirmation day.
Earlier duplicate-file comparison retained as preceding-review provenance, not claimed as an additional independently examined record in this pass.
unresolved: The exact number of days between testament and death is unread.
Husband’s forename is tentatively Niniane; no identity change is warranted solely by this pass.
Marioun’s relationship, the phrase after Jeane Meik, commodities, amounts and several witness/creditor names remain unresolved.
The confirmation day [27?] needs a further reading.
